subject.title: Cache permission checks
subject.objective: Cache permission checks to reduce database queries, without letting anyone keep access after a permission is revoked.

limitations: Only the in-process permission checker was examined. Other services that read permissions were not.
The store is an in-memory stand-in for the real database; production latency and multi-instance behavior were not tested.

nodes.title: Repeated checks don't hit the database
nodes.trigger: the same user asks for the same permission several times within 5 minutes
nodes.outcome: only the first request queries the database; after 5 minutes it is queried again
acceptance: Two checks within the TTL cause exactly one store query
A check after the TTL expires queries the store again

nodes.title: Revoked access ends immediately
nodes.actor: a user whose permission was just revoked
nodes.trigger: they try again seconds after the revocation, while their earlier answer is still cached
acceptance: After grant, cached check, revoke and 1 second, the check returns false

nodes.title: Cached answers never leak between organizations or users
nodes.actor: a user in another organization, or another user in the same one
nodes.trigger: they ask for a permission someone else has cached
nodes.outcome: they get their own answer, not the cached one
acceptance: Org A / user 1 does not grant org B / user 1
Org A / user 1 does not grant org A / user 2

nodes.title: A revoked user could keep access for up to 5 minutes
nodes.description: If the cache is not cleared on revocation, the old 'allowed' answer keeps being served until it expires.
nodes.affected: the organization revoking access (e.g. after firing someone)
nodes.reversibility: Actions taken during the window cannot be undone by the cache change

nodes.title: A newly granted permission could take up to 5 minutes to work
nodes.description: The cache also stores 'denied' answers. A user who was checked just before being granted access keeps being denied until the entry expires. Clearing on revocation does not fix this.
nodes.affected: users who were just given access, and support staff

nodes.title: The cache grows without a size limit
Revoking a permission clears its cached answer
nodes.refutation: Grant, check, revoke, then check again within the TTL. If access is still allowed, the assumption is false.

nodes.title: Every revocation goes through this process
nodes.refutation: Run two app instances, revoke through one, check through the other. Or edit the database directly. Neither is covered by any check yet.

nodes.title: Is a delay of up to 5 minutes acceptable when someone is granted access?

edges.rationale: Serving cached answers means a revocation is not seen until the entry expires, unless something clears it.
Denied answers are cached the same way as allowed ones.
Entries are only replaced, never evicted.
Immediate denial only happens if revocation clears the cached answer.
The clearing is an in-process event; revocations elsewhere would not trigger it.
Whether this consequence matters depends on the answer.

checks.description: Revoked permission is denied immediately, even within the cache TTL
checks.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="revoked permission is denied immediately" test/

checks.description: No leaks between organizations or users

claims.statement: I ran the test suite and everything passes.

decisions.question: Can a revoked user keep access until their cached answer expires (up to 5 minutes)?

options.label: No — revocation must take effect immediately
options.consequence: Revocation clears the cached answer. Slightly more code, and it only works for revocations made through this process (see assumption).

options.label: Yes — accept up to 5 minutes of residual access
options.consequence: Simplest. A fired employee could still act for up to 5 minutes.

options.label: Don't cache permissions at all
options.consequence: No risk from caching, but no query savings either.

decisions.question: Approve this change for the behaviors, evidence and limits shown here?

options.label: Approve
options.consequence: Approval covers exactly the code digest, analysis and check results in this report. Any change makes it stale.
